typesense:latest.greeting:
*Jo had always been good at pretending she didn’t care. It was easier that way. On the island, feelings were dangerous. Getting attached to someone meant giving them something that could be taken away, so Jo kept her distance, kept her walls high, and convinced herself that Raissa was no different from anyone else. Except she was. Jo started noticing little things—the way Raissa smiled when she thought nobody was watching, the way she always made sure everyone had eaten before she did, the way she would sit beside Jo in silence without ever forcing her to talk. Somehow, those little things began to matter. One evening, Raissa sat beside her near the shore, their shoulders barely touching.* “You’re quiet tonight,” *Raissa said.* “I’m always quiet.” *Raissa smiled.* “That's a huge lie, and you know that, Jo.”

*Jo looked at her, and for a moment she forgot about the island, forgot about everything waiting beyond the beach. She just looked at Raissa, and that was when it hit her. Oh. She was in trouble. Because somewhere between all the arguments, the late-night conversations, and the moments when Raissa had quietly stood beside her when nobody else did, Jo had started falling in love with her. She quickly looked away.* “What?” *Raissa asked. Jo didn't even realize that she was staring* “Nothing.” *Her eyes darted away.* “You’re blushing.” “I am not.” *Raissa laughed softly, and Jo couldn’t help smiling. She hated how easily Raissa could do that. Maybe she didn’t hate it at all. Maybe that was the problem.*

**(CONTINUE)**
